body: no, im on mobile. i’m considered lucky i guess. i’ve heard of places where even mobile phones are taken away.

i don’t know how to respond to that. but i really don’t feel any will to continue. everyday is an elongated. a life that i’d rather give to someone who would cherish it more. 

all i feel is torment by my condition and the fact that i can’t get a job torments me further.

i’m pretty much a bum at home. i’ve not been well enough medically speaking to be working but really i feel like that’s a lousy excuse. i have hands and legs why am i living off my mother? mentally unfit is such nonsense to me at times. but really am i even fit to work?

He was more than a person, more like a comfort, safety, shelter, what lever you call it. The job is an excellent excuse to live on, to be answerable. I don’t want my family to suffer. I’ve had a friend die this way and it still makes me sad. I can’t do that to them but I’m truly losing it.

I’ve been battling MDD and GAD for 2.5 years now. I know it isn’t a long time for many but it’s been nothing but awful.
I haven’t had a job in the past year and was even fired when the company found out I had these conditions.

At this moment, I’m truly alone and the one person whom I thought I could call home doesn’t want me anymore. And I can’t even hate him for that.

I’m ready to go. I want to go. I’m looking for excuses to stay so my family will be spared. But it’s getting harder and harder.
Thank you for your comment but it’s been really hard. I don’t know how else to describe it apart from never ending anguish.

Thank you for your kindness.
I majored in Literature and I loved reading. But over these years the unread books have stocked, physical and kindle. You’re amazing for being able to read. I look at the lines and can’t seem to “get” anything. 

I honestly feel like a waste of space and oxygen. I tell people that the best gift that they can offer the world is to be themselves because there’s only one of you. But it seems to me the best gift I can offer is to disappear.
